title: StrKey.encodeSignedPayload encodes a signed payload outside 1 to 64 bytes (empty or 65 bytes)
severity_basis: Encode side only: the SDK produces a P strkey SEP-23 calls invalid (an empty payload, or a 172-character strkey for a 65-byte payload); the 17.x decoder refuses both. No reader impact verified. Siblings are public in Go (open issue) and Rust (fixed).

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 0 bytes (SEP-23 and CAP-0040: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 16.4.1, 17.2.0, 17.2.1, 17.3.0 and 17.4.0: StrKey.encodeSignedPayload emits PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y for an empty payload instead of refusing it; the 17.x decoder refuses the text it emitted.

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 65 bytes (SEP-23 and CAP-0040: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 16.4.1, 17.2.0, 17.2.1, 17.3.0 and 17.4.0: StrKey.encodeSignedPayload emits a 172-character P strkey. The 16.x decoder reads it back; the 17.x decoder refuses it ('invalid encoded string length: expected 56-165, got 172').

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner, L4, on every JavaScript column: make verify-conformance (the 17.x columns) and xcc conform run --set public (the 16.x columns), entries strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-empty and strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-65-bytes.
evidence.expected_basis: SEP-23 (https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/f2d364902615af726b3533021403c8b225aa6e5d/ecosystem/sep-0023.md) and CAP-0040: a signed payload carries 1 to 64 bytes (opaque payload<64>), so its strkey is at most 165 characters; an empty payload or a 65-byte payload is invalid, and the SDK's own 17.x decoder refuses both.

reproduction.method: Independent reviewer reproduction from the record alone: the 7 empty-payload report rows failed again as recorded, offline. The 65-byte case was reproduced by the kit's run on 7 of 7 rows, offline, and checked by hand on 17.4.0 and main 81e76be before filing.

approval.scope: Public issue on stellar/js-stellar-sdk (#1899), covering the empty signed-payload encode and the 65-byte payload encode.

history.note: Created from the known divergences of strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-65-bytes that reference https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-sdk/issues/1899 and their failure rows.
The upstream item already records this defect.

Corrected: js-stellar-sdk#1899 was filed by the maintainers of this kit, so this record is the filing, not a duplicate of an existing item. Widened to the empty payload (strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-empty), which the same issue reports. No pull request (the repository takes pull requests by invitation).
